title: Pasritamig With Docetaxel vs Docetaxel in Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC)
official: A Phase 3 Randomized, Open-label Study of Pasritamig (JNJ-78278343), a T-cell-engaging Agent Targeting Human Kallikrein 2, With Docetaxel Versus Docetaxel for Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer
summary: Main objective: To determine whether treatment with pasritamig+docetaxel prolongs rPFS compared with docetaxel in participants with mCRPC

interventions.name: Docetaxel Hikma 20 mg/1 ml Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Infusionslösung
Docetaxel AqVida  20 mg/ml Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Infusionslösung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Have progressive metastatic castrate-resistant disease at the time of the screening defined as at least one of the following: - PSA level ≥2 ng/mL that has increased on at least 2 successive occasions at least 1 week apart. - Progressive disease or new lesion(s) in the lymph nodes or viscera on CT/MRI as defined by RECIST v1.1 and/or in bone on 99mTc bone scan per PCWG3 while on medical or surgical castration.
2. 2. Have progressed by PSA or CT/MRI or 99mTc bone scan on at least 1 novel ARPI but no more than 2 different ARPI (eg, abiraterone acetate, apalutamide, enzalutamide, darolutamide) for any stage of disease. Must have discontinued ARPI before randomization into the study.
3. 3. Have the following laboratory values during the screening period:   - Hemoglobin ≥9.0 g/dL  -  Neutrophils ≥1.5 x 10^9/L - Platelets ≥100 x 10^9/L Note, transfusion or growth factor usage within 14 days prior to randomization is not allowed.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Received cytotoxic chemotherapy for prostate cancer (eg, docetaxel, cabazitaxel, mitoxantrone, etc).
2. 2. Received prior treatment for prostate cancer with: - CD3 redirector therapies or - Radiopharmaceutical agents (eg, lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan, radium-223) or - Immunotherapy agents for prostate cancer (eg, sipuleucel-T, PD-1 inhibitors, T-cell redirectors, costimulatory agents, etc) or - PARP inhibitors (unless for BRCA1/2 mutations) or - Any other investigational agent for the treatment of mCRPC
3. 3. Patients with known BRCA 1/2 mutations (germline or somatic) who have not received treatment with a PARP inhibitor, unless not available or contraindicated.
